question: Stars twinkle at night due to:
solution:
The correct answer is the '**atmospheric refraction of starlight'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The stars seem to twinkle in the night sky due to **the effects of the Earth's atmosphere**.
 
• When starlight enters the atmosphere, it is affected by winds in the atmosphere and areas with different temperatures and densities.
 
• This causes the light from the star to twinkle when seen from the ground.
 
• 
 
when the light from a star passes through these different layers, it experiences different levels of refraction.

 
 
• 
 
Thus, the image of the star gets distorted constantly in brightness and position which makes the star look like its twinkling.
